metas.name: Agriculture - Blue Agave
metas.note:
Commonly known as the blue agave, A. tequilana is immediately recognisable by its blue, sharply protruding leaves. This is the agave from which tequila is extracted, and it mainly inhabits Jalisco, where it is almost always observed in magnificent fields which can even coalesce into vast shades of blue from a distance.

Similar, but different: A. anguistifolia.

While it is difficult to distinguish them, A. tequilana is noticeably bluer. One other difference is that A. angustifolia is more commonly spotted in isolated groupings than A. tequilana, but expansive fields still exist.

metas.name: Agriculture - Campeche Fields
metas.note: These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.

metas.name: Agriculture - Citrus Tree Plantation
metas.note: The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of citrus tree plantations. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.

metas.name: Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Agriculture - Prickly Pear Farm
metas.note: In the northeast most area of State of Mexico, around the town Nopaltepec, they often farm Opuntia in vast plains. Farms of prickly pear are otherwise most commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. These farms can be found randomly elsewhere in the country, but much less commonly; if there is a third most common location for them it would be Guanajuato.

metas.name: Agriculture - Pulque Agave Field
metas.note: One will often notice scattered farms of A. salmiana, gatherings which stretch limitlessly in neat rows; these will almost always be found around the city of Pachuca in Hidalgo, and rarely more south-east.

metas.name: Agriculture - Red Agricultural Fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.

metas.name: Agriculture - Very Dark Fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Architecture - Mud Brick
metas.note: Mud brick buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick. However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.

metas.name: Architecture - Northern Mexico Architecture
metas.note: Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows. Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards. Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

metas.name: Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Architecture - Thatched Roof
metas.note: Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi. They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

metas.name: Architecture - White Concrete Blocks
metas.note: White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east. They can however still be found all over the country.

metas.name: Car Meta - Cofre de Perote Truck
metas.note: This white truck with visible rearview mirrors can be seen in the Cofre de Perote national park.

metas.name: Car Meta - La Malinche Car
metas.note: This Street View car with a yellow hood can be found by the La Malinche volcano in Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Car Meta - La Seca Car
metas.note: This red Street View car with a black roof can be found in the town of La Seca in Sinaloa.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Asymmetric & Double-Stacked Insulator
metas.note: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.note:
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Blue Grain Pavement
metas.note:
Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature dashed outer lines.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cancun Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with five circular bulbs that looks like a dice is found in Cancun.

metas.name: Infrastructure - CDMX Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chihuahua Cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chihuahua Pole Paint
metas.note: Poles in Chihuahua city occasionally have a strip of white pole paint with the street name written in black or blue text.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cobblestone
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Cuernavaca Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a black rectangular head is found in Cuernavaca.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Durango Pole
metas.note: Poles with a lowered crossbar and a single support beam that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Eurus Wind Farm
metas.note: The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of wind turbines can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Green Bottom Pole
metas.note:
The bottom half of poles in Cuernavaca are often painted green.

NOTE: In Generation 4, the paint usually looks faded, some to the point where it is barely visible.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Concrete)
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Wooden)
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Hexagonal Tiles
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Jalisco Bollard
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Light Rock Wall
metas.note: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Matamoros Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a rectangular head and a ring-shaped light bulb is found in Matamoros.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Mesh Pole
metas.note: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Nayarit Bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oaxaca Pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Santiago de Queretaro Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle section is found in Santiago de Queretaro.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Tree Fences
metas.note:
These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz.

NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.

metas.name: Infrastructure - White Acorn Insulator
metas.note: White insulators that are shaped like acorns can be found along the coastal states of Mexico, but are by far most common in Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

metas.name: Infrastructure - White Roadlines
metas.note: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Wooden & Low Crossbar
metas.note: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Edge Road Divider
metas.note: This road divider with a yellow top and bottom edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Yellow Lamp Post
metas.note:
Most lamp posts and lamp arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow.

NOTE: They are not exclusive and are only very common.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Zig-Zag Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a zig-zag bent pole arm is found in Hermosillo.

metas.name: Landscape - Cerro del Bernal
metas.note: Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

metas.name: Landscape - Ciudad Juarez
metas.note: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.

metas.name: Landscape - Ciudad Obregon
metas.note: The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the pinkish-tan soil and canals found around the city’s agricultural areas.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal Cactus
metas.note: If you see a cactus in a coastal area, you're probably in Oaxaca.

metas.name: Landscape - Guaymas Cliffs
metas.note: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

metas.name: Landscape - Maderas del Carmen
metas.note:
This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.

metas.name: Landscape - MEX-40D
metas.note: The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

metas.name: Landscape - MEX-54
metas.note: The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.

metas.name: Landscape - Mexicali Landscape
metas.note: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.

metas.name: Landscape - Monterrey Mountains
metas.note: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.

metas.name: Landscape - Morelos Prickly Pear Farms
metas.note: Farms of prickly pear are commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground **striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. **

metas.name: Landscape - Northern Baja Landscape
metas.note: These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Landscape - Pink Lakes
metas.note: The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.

metas.name: Landscape - San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca
metas.note: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.

metas.name: Landscape - Sierra del Abra Tanchipa
metas.note: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Landscape - Twin Volcanoes
metas.note: The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.

metas.name: Landscape - Western Chi/Dur Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

metas.name: Landscape - White Soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave angustifolia
metas.note:
blue, but less blue than tequilana, smaller grouping

found in Central Oaxaca

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave Asperrina
metas.note: The rough century plant looks similar to the pulque agave but its leaves are blueish and it is much smaller. It is distributed nearly identically to A. lechuguilla (Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and West of Torreon, rarely SLP and Hidalgo), and is often difficult to spot from the road, only barely visible in the distance in batches.

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave Cupreata
metas.note: Agave cupreata is a very rarely observed agave that is localised to central Guerrero. Its name is apt - it has a much more pronounced, cup-like appearance than other agaves, with the leaves lurching inwards. It is often found growing on walls in groups as depicted.

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave Karwinskii
metas.note: A. karwinskii is exclusively seen in the central desert region of Oaxaca, mostly near the town Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz, even though technically its native distribution extends elsewhere in the state and barely into Puebla. Its spiky thin leaves, protruding from the centre in a cylindrical formation, make it quite distinct from other common agaves.

metas.name: Vegetation - Agave Lechuguilla
metas.note: Agave lechuguilla is a very frequent sighting in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, particularly around the cities of Saltillo and west of Torreon. More rarely it can be found in San Luis Potosi and Hidalgo. It is distinguished by its slick, lime-green leaves that almost look as if they are combed to one side.

metas.name: Vegetation - Blue Myrtle Cactus
metas.note: Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Boojum Tree
metas.note: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Vegetation - Brittlebush
metas.note: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.

metas.name: Vegetation - Candelabro
metas.note: Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Cephalocereus Mezcalaensis
metas.note: This tall, columnar cactus, with no branches, is native to northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla, and another of the many species present there. Much less commonly but still possibly it can be seen in central Guerrero.

metas.name: Vegetation - Chiotilla
metas.note: The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.note: Coconut palms can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.

metas.name: Vegetation - Florida Thach palm
metas.note:
This palm is recognizable through its round fan leaves.

Within Mexico, it's usually found in Yucatan.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Fruit Cholla
metas.note: The golden glow of the fruit cholla is also unmistakable, and present mostly in the Western Half of Sonora.

metas.name: Vegetation - Giant Cardon
metas.note: Pachycereus pringlei is a species of large cactus native to northwestern Mexico, in the states of Baja California, Baja California Sur. It can rarely be found on the Sonoran coast, around the area south of Puerto Libertad on the 3.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Vegetation - Golden Line
metas.note: These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.

metas.name: Vegetation - Indian Comb
metas.note: The Indian Comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum), is a common cactus that always implies Sinaloa, or south Sonora near Sinaloa, although technically its habitat extends elsewhere. Its densely packed branches emerge from a single stem, but most recognisable is its inflorescence - the brightly coloured flowers which usually adorn the tip of its arms.

metas.name: Vegetation - Organ Pipe Cactus
metas.note: This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. If the cactus is significantly larger than 3m, it's probably in Southern Baja.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Organ Pipe Spam
metas.note: A huge abundance of Organ Pipe Cacti it is usually indicative of the reserve El Cajón del Diablo, south of Hermosillo.

metas.name: Vegetation - Pitaya de Querétaro
metas.note:
In Pitaya the branches less organically sprout from the ground in the weed-like manner of the Organ Pipe, and instead curl smoothly outwards from a central stem.

It is mostly found in Jalisco, south of Guadalajara. Less commonly, it's seen in Guanajuato. It can be seen in Queretaro too, but surprisingly rarely.

metas.name: Vegetation - Prickly Pear alone
metas.note: Prickly pear cacti with a total absence of other cacti, yucca, agaves or in general succulent plants except for the prickly pear is generally a good signal for the centre-west (Jalisco, Guanajuato, Michoacan).

metas.name: Vegetation - Prickly Pear Cactus
metas.note:
Prickly pear cacti are distinct with their flat oval-shaped pads. They are noticeably more common centrally and are rarely seen in southern and coastal states.

They are also good for some 50/50:

  • Durango > Chihuahua
  • Durango > Sonora (less reliable)
  • Nuevo Leon > Tamaulipas
  • Other States > Mexico State
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Vegetation - Pulque Agave
metas.note:
Agave salmiana, colloquially the pulque agave, is native to central Mexico. Agaves in general are distinguishable by their crown-like appearance, with stiff leaves which fan outwards symmetrically. The pulque agave is no different, but has green leaves, relatively smooth edges, and flat leaves that curl slightly away from the central axis.

Note its distribution, in an arc around Mexico City and a second pocket of endemism which straddles San Luis Potosi city and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Vegetation - Quintana Roo Tree
metas.note: These thin, white-barked trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.

metas.name: Vegetation - Sabal Mexicana
metas.note:
This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Sabal Rosei
metas.note:
Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Sabal Yapa
metas.note:
This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Saguaro
metas.note: The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Stenocereus fricii
metas.note: A rare and tall cactus, the thin and twirling branches of S. fricii are unique to Michoacan, especially on the 37D, where it is abundantly spammed.

metas.name: Vegetation - Tlaxcala Bois
metas.note: These clumps of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Vegetation - Tree Cholla
metas.note:
The tree cholla is a cactus, and its skeletal, discoloured arms spurting in every direction make it recognisable.

Mostly found in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango and rarely in Zacatecas.

metas.name: Vegetation - Tree Cholla Group
metas.note: If it is present in groups, Tree Cholla is usually a good indication of San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Vegetation - Tree Yucca
metas.note: It is native to central mexico, most commonly found in Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí although it can be seen anywhere from Nuevo León down to Puebla, in dry regions.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Vegetation - Umbrella Palm
metas.note: The Attalea rostrata is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.

metas.name: Vegetation - Unknown Cactus
metas.note: Oaxaca is very diverse in Cacti, so if you see a strange cactus, or one that isn't explained in this map, you can consider going Oaxaca.
